sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax in Kent County, Michigan?
sections.html:
In Kent County the bill comes from the city or township where the house sits, and the county treasurer takes over only after a tax goes delinquent. The county's Bureau of Equalization does not set your value. It makes sure assessments stay uniform across the 21 townships and nine cities in the county, and the local assessor does the actual valuing.

That split matters when you have a question. A wrong value, a missing exemption or a bill that never arrived is a question for the local assessor or local treasurer. A tax that was returned unpaid is the Kent County Treasurer's business, and that office also sells foreclosed parcels after a court order. The treasurer's counter is in the Kent County Administration Building at 300 Monroe Avenue NW in Grand Rapids, open Monday through Friday, 8 am to 5 pm.

sections.h2: What does Kent County look like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Kent County is the largest county in Michigan outside the Detroit area, with Grand Rapids as both county seat and largest city. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 675,232 residents, and the 2020-2024 survey counts 256,648 households.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $289,900
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 70.3%
  • Median household income: $82,631
  • Median gross rent: $1,243

With a typical home near $290,000, a late balance grows into real money fast, because the penalties below are percentages of the unpaid bill. Every parcel in the county follows the same collection calendar, whether it is in a city or a township.

sections.h2: When do unpaid Kent County property taxes become delinquent, and what do they cost?
sections.html:
Taxes left unpaid on March 1 of the following year are returned to the county treasurer, who adds a 4% administration fee and interest of 1% per month. Kent County's own FAQ says the local treasurers bill on July 1 and December 1, and that there is no provision to waive the fees, even if a bill never reached you.

Summer bills have an earlier pinch point. Under MCL 211.44a, interest is added to summer taxes collected after September 14. The steps after that follow a fixed state calendar:

Kent County delinquent tax steps and added costs (Kent County Treasurer FAQ; MCL 211.78a)
StageTimingWhat is added
Returned delinquentMarch 1 after the tax year4% fee plus 1% interest per month
ForfeitureMarch 1, one year later$175 title search fee, $60 recording fees, interest rises to 1.5% per month
Foreclosure preparationMarch 31 after the forfeiture dateProperty is readied for a foreclosure judgment

The county sums it up as two years and one month to pay before foreclosure. Its auction list of foreclosed properties appears around July 1 each year.

sections.h2: How can an owner pay delinquent taxes to the Kent County Treasurer?
sections.html:
You can pay online, by phone, by mail, through the Kent County mobile app, or at the counter. Have the parcel number or street address ready for any method.

  • Online: E-check from a bank account has a $0 fee. Credit cards add 2.98%, collected by the card processor and not by the county.
  • Phone: 616-303-7760, option 1 for English or option 2 for Spanish, cards only, with the same processing fee.
  • Mail: Checks or money orders payable to Kent County Treasurer, P.O. Box Y, Grand Rapids, MI 49501-4925, with the parcel ID written on the memo line.
  • In person: The counter is meant for transactions that require cash. Others are encouraged to pay online or by mail.

Partial payments are accepted at any time, but fees and interest keep running on the unpaid balance. Kent County does not honor postmarks. The payment has to arrive before the end of a month to count at that month's payoff figure, so call 616-632-7500 for the current payoff before sending a check.

sections.h2: Can a Kent County owner delay foreclosure with a hardship deferral?
sections.html:
Yes, for up to one year, if the owner qualifies and applies in time. The county's Financial Hardship program is open to someone who holds title by recorded deed or land contract, lives in the home as a principal residence, and can show substantial financial hardship.

The application asks for a payment plan on page 3. A plan can include regular payments or a record of them, help from a local assistance agency, or the sale or refinancing of the property. The form must be in before March 1, and the treasurer's office does not promise approval. A deferral is also a one-time tool, and it does not reduce the bill: interest and fees continue to pile up during the extension.

For a homeowner who plans to sell, that last point is the one to weigh. The deferral buys time to close a sale, and the balance still comes out of the sale price.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Kent County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the assessor in your city or township, then take the case to that unit's March board of review. The treasurer's FAQ tells owners who think the taxable value is too high to contact the local assessor, since the county does not hear valuation appeals.

State law (MCL 211.30) has the board of review meet on the second Monday in March, with a city or township allowed to start on the Tuesday or Wednesday after. The board must sit at least 12 hours that week, and a person who files a protest is entitled to written notice of the result by the first Monday in June, along with information on the right to go on to the Michigan Tax Tribunal. A separate July and December board only handles qualified errors and a few specific exemption appeals (MCL 211.53b), and it can correct the current and prior year only.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and relief programs apply in Kent County?
sections.html:
The big ones are the Principal Residence Exemption and the poverty exemption. The PRE removes the local school operating tax, up to 18 mills, from a home that its owner occupies as a principal residence. You claim it at the local assessor's office, on or before June 1 for the summer bill or November 1 for the winter bill, and the county FAQ sends a denial from the state to the Michigan Department of Treasury for an informal conference, and a denial from the local unit or county to the Michigan Tax Tribunal.

For the poverty exemption, the county points owners to the city or township assessor. The state's homestead property tax credit is a different program, filed with the Michigan income tax return. If your mortgage company escrows taxes, check your statements anyway, because the Kent County treasurer notes that a missed escrow payment is a common cause of delinquency and that the owner is the one responsible for confirming the tax gets paid.

sections.h2: What happens with property tax when a Kent County house sells?
sections.html:
Delinquent tax has to be cleared for most deeds to record, and a sale resets the taxable value. Under MCL 211.135, a register of deeds requires a county treasurer certificate that no tax liens exist and that taxes for the previous five years are paid, and Kent County's register of deeds charges $5 per deed for that certification on warranty deeds and land contracts. A quitclaim deed with no warranty covenants is excepted from that rule.

After a transfer, MCL 211.27a resets the taxable value to the state equalized value in the following year, which can raise the buyer's bill. The buyer has 45 days to file the property transfer notice with the local assessing office. If you owe Kent County tax and want a sale without repairs or showings, the closing agent can pay the payoff figure from your proceeds once the treasurer confirms the amount.

faqs.q: When does Kent County start charging interest on unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Interest begins on summer taxes collected after September 14, and the county adds its own fee on March 1. That date comes from MCL 211.44a. On March 1 the Kent County Treasurer adds a 4% administration fee and 1% interest per month to anything left unpaid, and the county FAQ says none of these charges can be waived.

faqs.q: How long before Kent County can foreclose on a house for unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: About two years and one month. Taxes become delinquent March 1, the property is forfeited on the following March 1, and foreclosure preparation begins March 31 after that. The Kent County Treasurer conducts the sale of properties more than 24 months delinquent after a court order.

faqs.q: Does the hardship deferral lower what I owe Kent County?
faqs.a: No. The deferral only delays the foreclosure deadline by up to one year. Interest and fees continue to accumulate, and the application has to be submitted before March 1 with a plan for paying the taxes.

faqs.q: Who do I call to fight my assessment in Kent County?
faqs.a: Call the assessor for your city or township first. The county treasurer does not change values, and valuation appeals go to the local March board of review, then to the Michigan Tax Tribunal if you disagree with the result.

faqs.q: Do I have to pay Kent County back taxes before I sell?
faqs.a: Usually yes, at closing at the latest. A warranty deed needs a treasurer certificate of taxes paid for the past five years, so the delinquent balance is normally paid from the sale proceeds. Call 616-632-7500 for the exact payoff before you set a closing date.
